c0784: Buy your paella pans, 3-ring burners and propane kit, and test every ring
c0787: Buy pans in three sizes: 36 in (90 cm), 32 in (80 cm) and 26 in (65 cm), plus 3-ring burners with legs. Light each ring, check the regulator and hoses with soapy water, and run a full cook before your first event. Add eight 20-lb cylinders with regulators and hoses within their date, two extinguishers and a fire blanket, and open an account with a propane refill or exchange service.
c0842: Set your service charge and gratuity policy
c0845: A mandatory service charge is not a tip: the part paid out to staff is wages (IRS Rev. Rul. 2012-18). A gratuity is voluntary and goes to staff. Keep them on separate invoice lines and check your state's sales tax rule.
c0858: Train service protocol: the socarrat reveal, uniform, briefing and the nine major allergens
c0861: Run a pre-event briefing every time. The nine major US allergens include fish and crustacean shellfish (crab, lobster, shrimp); label mussels and clams too. Watch for egg in the aioli, wheat in the bread and noodle paella, sulfites in frozen shrimp, and cross-contact from shared paddles and pans. Send allergy questions to the paella chef.
c0884: Define your tasting policy for prospects
c0887: Decide who gets a tasting, how many guests attend and whether the fee is credited toward the booking. Track the bookings each tasting produces.
c0888: Create a proposal template with the kit calculator and track leads in your CRM
c0891: Build your quote in the pricing calculator: pans by size, rice per guest and the shopping list; the template turns it into a polished quote. Log every inquiry and follow up within 48 hours. Pick catering software that sends the quote, collects the e-signature and takes the deposit by card or ACH.
c0892: Prospect corporate clients: office managers, HR and event planners
c0895: Build a list of nearby offices and drop off sample lunches. Repeat weekday orders make your base, so follow up every contact.
